paragraphs: Our Rainy Plan, posted by Lily. The Explorers planned a trip to the nature park. We had our notebooks and our bags ready. But the weather changed our plan. It rained for four days, so the paths were wet. On Wednesday, Teacher Kim received an email from Ranger Mark. He wrote, "The forest is wet, and the path is not safe." We were not happy, but we understood.

On Thursday, we had our club hour as usual. "What else can we do?" asked Mia. "We cannot walk in the forest, but we can learn about it online," said Leo. Teacher Kim liked the idea. She gave us a link to a video about a forest. We watched it on the library computer. May asked many questions, and Teacher Kim answered them. The video was short, but we learned a lot.

The rain stopped on Friday. But the paths were still wet on Saturday. Because we could not go to the park, we met in the gym. The gym was big and quiet. First, we did some exercise, because we wanted to move. Then we sat on the floor with our notebooks. Mia drew a bird, and Leo made a cartoon of a wet tree. May wrote questions for Ranger Mark, so he can answer them next month.

"Many birds make nests in tall trees, but some make nests on the ground," read Mia. "The ground is not safe when it rains," said Lily. "That is true, because water comes into the nest," said Teacher Kim. "Do birds like rain?" asked Leo. "Some birds like it, because they can find food," said Teacher Kim. We wrote this fact on our page. Leo added a small picture.

We cannot visit the forest this month, but we will go next month. Click the link under this post, and you can see Mia's photos. You can see Leo's cartoon, too. Thank you, Ranger Mark, for your email. Our rainy plan was not bad, because we learned many things. What do you do on a rainy day?
